content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper present a method for encoding spatiotemporal information from 3D skeleton data based on motion energy for enhancing skeleton-based action recognition. The approach uses the skeleton representation by Ahmed et al. 2015 to compute motion energy using approach proposed by Liu et al 2017c. The approach is evaluated on home-grown online action dataset and the performance is comparable to some recent approaches.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
The idea of encoding joints based on the motion energy.

Weakness:
Lack of novelty.
Authors have not considered the recent advances in skeleton-based action recognition
Experimental evaluation and comparison to the state-of-the-art approaches
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is written well and clearly mention the problem in 3D skeleton-based action recognition. The authors should look into the state-of-the-art works on skeleton-driven action recognition. Some of the recent works are:

Song, Yi-Fan, et al. "Constructing stronger and faster baselines for skeleton-based action recognition." IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (2022).
Haodong Duan, Yue Zhao, Kai Chen, Dahua Lin, Bo Dai; Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2022, pp. 2969-2978
Yuxin Chen, Ziqi Zhang, Chunfeng Yuan, Bing Li, Ying Deng, Weiming Hu; Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2021, pp. 13359-13368
Yukun Su, Guosheng Lin, Qingyao Wu; Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2021, pp. 13328-13338
Tianjiao Li, Qiuhong Ke, Hossein Rahmani, Rui En Ho, Henghui Ding, Jun Liu; Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2021, pp. 13434-13443
Mazzia, Vittorio, et al. "Action Transformer: A self-attention model for short-time pose-based human action recognition." Pattern Recognition 124 (2022): 108487.
Guo, Tianyu, et al. "Contrastive learning from extremely augmented skeleton sequences for self-supervised action recognition." Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence. Vol. 36. No. 1. 2022.

The paper is very basic experimental evaluation and is not appropriate for the top conference such as ICLR.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper has identified the problems in 3D skeleton-based action recognition. The work is very basic and is evaluated on a home-grown dataset. The paper does not consider the recent advances in skeleton-based action recognition and should explore these approaches and clearly mention the advance in knowledge. The work is at the early stage and improve it based on the state-of-the-art approaches and submit to the future conferences.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper investigates the approach to encoding 3D skeletons into spatio-temporal images as input for activity recognition. The proposed method combines the idea of motion energy [Liu et al. 2017c] to weigh the color of the SpatioTemporal Image Encoding [Mokhtari et al. 2022]. The authors examine two approaches for weighting, frame-by-frame and sequence-level weights. They evaluated their approach through an experiment using the OAD dataset and concluded that the approach combining both original and frame-by-frame motion encodings achieved the best performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The proposed idea is reasonable, and clearly presented throughout the paper.

Weaknesses
- The method is a relatively straightforward combination of prior work, and the technical novelty is not significant. The text also has considerable overlap with the prior work [Mokhtari et al. 2022].
- Comparative experiments are not sufficient. It is not clear why only the OAD data set is used for evaluation, and the performance of the baseline methods there is only the ones taken from [Liu et al. 2019]. Furthermore, the numbers cited here are the results of action prediction at a 90% observation rate, so it does not seem appropriate in this experimental setting.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The method is simple, and the paper provides sufficient information to reimplement the method. 
- The novelty lies in the combination of motion energy and STIE, which shows an improvement in performance from the original STIE feature. The significance and benefits of image encoding itself have not been fully discussed, and comparisons with skeleton-based baseline methods are weak.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the technical novelty and its effectiveness have not been adequately demonstrated. The manuscript in its current state does not reach the level of acceptance.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a spatial-temporal image encoding of 3d skeletons for human activity recognition.  It combines the image encoding from Mokhtari 2022 and motion energy from Liu 2017. It uses the ImageNet pre-trained models to initialize the activity recognition models. The proposed method is evaluated on the OAD dataset and compared with other methods. The results are good.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

The motivation for image encoding of 3d skeletons is good, and many image-trained models can be used for training activity models. The experiment results on OAD data in table 5 are good using the retraining of the VGG16 model.  


Weaknesses:

The theoretical novelties are not clear. The image encoding part is from  Mokhtari 2022 and the motion energy between two consecutive frames is from Liu 2017. The related work section is too long. Compared with the related works, the novelties of this paper can be mentioned in this related work section.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The writing of this paper needs a lot of improvements.  For example, the length of the related work section can be shorter. The novelties of the current version of this paper are not enough. It would be great if the authors can release their code. It is hard to reproduce their results.
content.summary_of_the_review: The novelties of this paper are insufficient for being accepted. In addition, the writing of this paper needs to be improved.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
- The paper proposes to use a spatio-temporal image encoding of 3D skeletons for the task of online human activity recognition
- To do so, they provide a study on the concept of motion energy to focus on skeleton joints that are the most relevant for a particular action. 
- Provide benchmark results using various pre-trained CNNs
- Using their approach leads to an improvement on one dataset
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths : 
- The paper targets a relevant area of computer vision research - action recognition using skeleton sequences. 
- The idea of focusing on relevant joints is an interesting one and various 


Weaknesses:
- Related works and comparisons with prior works : The paper does a poor job of discussing related works. The area of action recognition using skeletons has seen a lot of interest the past few years. While I do not expect the paper to cite every paper, it does not do a good job putting itself in the context of others and providing similarities and differences. Some feedback on how to improve this section :
    - The section on graphs for encoding skeletons does not discuss the more recent techniques. Please include a paragraph on why graph-based techniques were not considered for your work. 
    - Representing skeleton as images : Missing works like PoTion[a], SkeleMotion[b], techniques which represent skeleton joints using heatmaps like : PA3D[c]
    - Approaches which improve pose based action recognition, for example by focusing on various joints [d], 3D-CNNs [e]
    - Page 3, "A limitation of this work includes Online Action Recognition (OAR) task" -- Unclear why this is a limitation. 
    - Figure 5 : Please include details in the caption regarding "this reordering allows to create spatio-temporal neighborhoods in the image"

- Organization of the paper, presentation and clarity :
    - The paper is not well organized and has a lot of white space, oversized figures - a lot of this could be used to improve captions, text etc. 
    - Figure 1 is unnecessary and does not add any new information - Please move this to supplementary. Instead add a figure explaining your solution to the problem as the first figure of the paper. 
    - I would suggest moving the explanations for the papers Mokhtaru et al and Liu et al into a separate section titled preliminaries.
    - Please do not use "<< .. >>" to highlight. An alternative is to use \emph{} 

- Experimental results & Method :
   - The method is a simple combination of two prior works - while simplicity could be a strength, the paper should clearly explain its contributions. 
   - It is essential to compare the approach to other skeleton-action based approaches (graph & image based) on standard benchmark datasets (like NTU and PKU) 
   - How expensive is the model ? Can the model run real-time. Please include metrics like FLOPs, parameter count, memory requirement. 
   - What happens if you train a model from scratch ? How about smaller models ? 


[a] PoTion: Pose MoTion Representation for Action Recognition - CVPR 2018
[b] SkeleMotion: A New Representation of Skeleton Joint Sequences Based on Motion Information for 3D Action Recognition - AVSS 2019
[c] PA3D: Pose-Action 3D Machine for Video Recognition - CVPR 2019
[d] Pose And Joint-Aware Action Recognition - WACV 2022
[e] Revisiting Skeleton-based Action Recognition - CVPR 2022
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- While many parts of the paper are clear, the organization of the paper needs some work to enhance clarity. 
- Novelty is lacking - It combines two prior works. Experiments on a single dataset leave questions on whether the approach could be useful for other more common datasets in this area. 

Please refer to the section on strengths and weaknesses for additional comments.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I think that the paper still needs work. It is limited on novelty. It has issues with clarity, experimental evaluation, comparison to prior work. I hope that the feedback is helpful to improve the paper.

content.title: Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Image Encoding for Online Human Activity Recognition
content.TL;DR: In this work, we propose to improve the spatio-temporal image encoding of 3D skeletons data, by studying the concept of motion energy which focuses mainly on the joints that are the most solicited for an action.
content.abstract:
Human Activity Recognition (HAR) based on sensors data can be seen as a time series classification problem where the challenge is to handle both spatial and temporal dependencies, while focusing on the most relevant data variations. It can be done using 3D skeleton data extracted from a RGB+D camera.
In this work, we propose to improve the spatio-temporal image encoding of 3D skeletons captured from a Kinect sensor, by studying the concept of motion energy which focuses mainly on skeleton joints that are the most solicited for an action. This encoding allows us to achieve a better discrimination for the detection of online activities by focusing on the most significant parts of the actions.
The article presents this new encoding and its application for HAR using a deep learning model trained on the encoded 3D skeleton data.
For this purpose, we proposed to investigate the knowledge transferability of several pre-trained CNNs provided by Keras.
The article shows a significant improvement of the accuracy of the learning according to the state of the art.
